question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Reference class puts the median 10-session WTI-minus-SPX spread near zero (slightly negative: front-month oil has ~no drift, equities have positive drift). The 2026 war regime widens dispersion enormously but does not clearly shift the center. Bearish-spread: oil just added 9.7% in a week on headlines and every 2026 spike partially retraced (Apr 8 ceasefire crashed WTI ~16-20% in a day); EIA's Aug 11 STEO puts Brent Q3 at $85 vs spot $95.29 and assumes Hormuz flows 'slowly increasing in September'; Polymarket's downside barriers imply higher vol than its upside ones, i.e. the market itself prices the fatter tail as a peace-driven collapse, with much of the war premium already in the price. Bullish-spread: strikes resumed, Vance ruled out talks until Iran stops attacking Hormuz shipping, Israel threatened 'crippling' strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, JMIC rates Hormuz 'severe' with mine risk, Q3 inventories drawing 3.8 mb/d; and the equity leg faces PPI (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11) and a 58-66%-priced hike at the Sep 15-16 FOMC under a hawkish Warsh Fed, plus the weakest month seasonally. These offset, so I stay near the base rate at -1.0 and spend my effort on width. Both bounds are open and both escapes have named mechanisms with 2026 precedent (a 35% weekly WTI gain in March, a 16% one-day drop in April), so I price them at 5%/6% rather than the ~1-2% a Gaussian would give.

calls.reference_class: Non-overlapping 10-trading-day windows, 2000-2026, of front-month WTI crude futures price return minus S&P 500 futures price return; sub-class weighted toward 2026's Iran-war/Hormuz-disruption regime, where realized WTI dispersion is roughly triple its long-run norm

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day return differentials of front-month WTI futures minus S&P 500 futures. Unconditional historical median is about -0.4pp (equity drift ~+0.5%/2wk beats oil's ~+0.1%); conditioned on high-vol geopolitical supply regimes (OVX>40) the median is similar but dispersion roughly doubles. That conditional class is the one that binds: OVX ~47 vs VIX ~14.5 means oil supplies ~95% of the spread variance, so the distribution is wide (10-90 ~23pp) and right-skewed. Center: I hold the median slightly negative. Oil just added 9.7% in a week on a risk premium, not a realized barrel loss - Hormuz throughput was near 7 mb/d late August and Iraqi southern exports averaged 2.35 mb/d in August and are set to rise - and geopolitical premia decay absent actual supply loss; three prior de-escalations this year (Apr 8 ceasefire, Jun 17 memorandum) show the reversal channel is live. Against that: an intact technical breakout above ~$91.35, Israeli threats against Iranian energy infrastructure, and an equity leg facing CPI 9/11 plus an FOMC 9/15-16 with ~52-58% hike odds into record highs and the weakest seasonal stretch - which is why I only shade the median to -0.8 rather than -1.5, and why the mean sits positive at +0.8. Escape mass: +25pp needs Hormuz closure or a strike on Iranian export infrastructure (5%); -25pp needs a credible durable peace collapsing a ~$20-25/bbl war premium in ten sessions (3%). Evidence is one-sided toward escalation headlines but thin on any confirmed physical supply loss, so I stay close to the reference-class center with wide bands.

calls.reconciliation: Centers were never in dispute (-1.0/-0.8/-1.0); I carry that forward at -0.9. The real disputes were width and left-tail mass. On width I took Run 3's FRED-measured daily SDs over Runs 1-2's remembered annualized vols (same series, actually retrieved), but rejected its 21 because its zero-correlation assumption understates tail width when both dominant scenarios move the legs oppositely; I also rejected Run 1's 28 as extrapolated from the March-May OVX-108 regime that the Sep 3 OVX of 46 says has passed. Landed at 23 - inside the members' range because the reconciled arithmetic puts it there, not as a compromise. On the left tail I took 3%: Run 1's 6% rests on a Polymarket touch-ladder skew reading I discount as a barrier-distance artifact (crisis-regime crude normally carries call, not put, skew), while Run 3's 2% underweights that a June MOU already materialized once out of nowhere this year. Factual checks that stuck: OVX 46.41 (Sep 3, FRED) supersedes the Aug 18 47.17 both other runs used; the Sep 5 'WTI at three-month low' headline is stale or mis-dated against four Sep 4-6 reports of a $91.48 six-month-high settle; OPEC+ met Sep 6 and left October unchanged with no further meeting in-window, which I accept as uncontradicted. Two disputes I could NOT settle without web access and which I let the width absorb rather than resolve by fiat: (a) whether a volume-based front-month roll lands Sep 15-17 - all runs agree CLV26 expires ~Sep 22, but the question's criteria field is empty so the series is unverified, worth a fraction of a point in backwardation; (b) Hormuz throughput, where 4.9, ~7 and ~17 mb/d are quoted and are almost certainly not the same quantity, leaving genuinely open how much supply is still at risk. Escape masses: I agreed with all three runs' 5% upside; the mechanism and the July +28.5% precedent are the same evidence for all of us.

disagreements.claim: Hormuz throughput is 4.9 vs ~7 vs ~17 mb/d
disagreements.verdict: Unsettleable - the three figures are near-certainly different quantities (EIA quarterly crude average, a late-August crude estimate, and total escorted transits). Left as genuine uncertainty about remaining at-risk supply; contributes to width.

disagreements.claim: OPEC+ met Sep 6 and held October output unchanged, next meeting Oct 4
disagreements.verdict: Accepted (Run 3 only, uncontradicted). Removes one scheduled in-window downside catalyst for the oil leg.

disagreements.verdict: Settled at 3%. Run 1's Polymarket downside-skew evidence discounted as a barrier artifact; Run 3's 2% underweights the demonstrated 2026 pattern of surprise de-escalation (Apr 8 ceasefire, Jun 17 MOU).

No material dispute (-1.0/-0.8/-1.0); reconciled at -0.9. Premium-decay after a headline-driven +10% week and positive equity drift pull down; FOMC hike odds, CPI, September seasonality and widening escalation pull up; they roughly cancel.
